name: Edward VIII
blurb: King of the United Kingdom who abdicated after less than a year on the throne (1894–1972) · gave up the crown in 1936 to marry the twice-divorced American Wallis Simpson, then spent the war years as governor of the Bahamas, kept deliberately far from Britain
attribution: Attributed to Angelo Laviosa / Formerly attributed to Vincenzo Laviosa
source: Wikimedia Commons: Duke and Duchess of Windsor - Google Art Project (Duke cropped).jpg
image_author: Attributed to Angelo Laviosa / Formerly attributed to Vincenzo Laviosa

name: Stanley Kubrick
blurb: American film director notorious for punishing perfectionism (1928–1999) · made Shelley Duvall reshoot one hallway scene in The Shining 127 times, a still-standing record for the most takes of a single scene with dialogue
attribution: Phillip A. Harrington, an American photographer and staffer for Look magazine between 1949–1971
source: Wikimedia Commons: Stanley Kubrick (1949 portrait by Phillip Harrington - cropped).jpg
image_author: Phillip A. Harrington, an American photographer and staffer for Look magazine between 1949–1971

name: Edward VII
blurb: King of the United Kingdom who waited 59 years as Prince of Wales before taking the throne (1841–1910) · Queen Victoria kept him out of state business for nearly the entire wait, so he filled the decades with racehorses, mistresses, and cigars instead
source: Wikimedia Commons: King-Edward-VII (cropped).jpg

name: Bruce Lee
blurb: Martial artist and actor who brought kung fu to global screens (1940–1973) · won Hong Kong's cha-cha dancing championship in 1958, years before he ever threw an on-screen punch
source: Wikimedia Commons: Bruce Lee 1973 (cropped).jpg

name: George Orwell
blurb: English writer and journalist behind 1984 and Animal Farm (1903–1950) · born Eric Arthur Blair, he was shot through the throat by a sniper while fighting in the Spanish Civil War and survived
source: Wikimedia Commons: George Orwell, c. 1940 (41928180381).jpg

name: Andrew Jackson
blurb: Seventh president of the United States (1767–1845) · his pet parrot, Poll, had to be carried out of Jackson's own funeral for swearing at the mourners
source: Wikimedia Commons: Andrew jackson head.jpg

name: Agatha Christie
blurb: British crime novelist behind Poirot and Miss Marple (1890–1976) · vanished for 11 days in 1926, sparking a nationwide manhunt, and never once explained what happened
source: Wikimedia Commons: Agatha Christie in Nederland (detectiveschrijfster), bij aankomst op Schiphol me, Bestanddeelnr 916-8898 (cropped).jpg

name: Moses
blurb: Biblical lawgiver who led the Exodus from Egypt (traditionally c. 13th century BC) · painters for centuries gave him small horns, like the ones visible here, a literal mistranslation of the Hebrew word for his radiant face
source: Wikimedia Commons: Philippe de Champaigne - Moses Presenting the Tablets of the Law - c. 1648.jpg

name: Pope John Paul II
blurb: Polish pope who led the Catholic Church for over 26 years (1920–2005) · survived being shot four times in St Peter's Square in 1981, then visited his would-be assassin in prison to forgive him face to face
source: Wikimedia Commons: Pope John Paul II smile.jpg

name: John Wayne
blurb: American film actor who became the face of the Western (1907–1979) · picked up the nickname 'Duke' as a boy, after his pet Airedale terrier of the same name, not any horse
source: Wikimedia Commons: John Wayne - still portrait.jpg

name: Franz Kafka
blurb: Bohemian writer of The Trial and The Metamorphosis (1883–1924) · asked his friend Max Brod to burn all his unpublished manuscripts after his death; Brod ignored him and published them instead
source: Wikimedia Commons: Kafka1906 cropped.jpg

name: Nikita Khrushchev
blurb: Soviet premier who steered the USSR through the Cuban Missile Crisis (1894–1971) · reportedly banged his shoe on the table during a 1960 UN General Assembly session to protest a delegate's remarks
source: Wikimedia Commons: Nikita Khrushchev official portrait.jpg

name: Paul the Apostle
blurb: Early Christian missionary whose letters make up much of the New Testament (c. 5 – c. 65 AD) · once a zealous persecutor of Christians named Saul, he converted after being struck blind on the road to Damascus
source: Wikimedia Commons: Giovanni Francesco Barbieri - Saint Paul.jpg

name: Henry Kissinger
blurb: American diplomat and secretary of state under Nixon and Ford (1923–2023) · shared the 1973 Nobel Peace Prize for a Vietnam ceasefire that collapsed within two years; his Vietnamese co-winner refused to accept his half
attribution: U.S. Department of State from United States
source: Wikimedia Commons: Henry A. Kissinger, U.S. Secretary of State, 1973-1977.jpg
image_author: U.S. Department of State from United States

name: George III
blurb: King of Great Britain during the loss of the American colonies (1738–1820) · recurring bouts of mental illness once saw him reportedly bow to an oak tree in Windsor Great Park, mistaking it for the King of Prussia
source: Wikimedia Commons: Allan Ramsay (1713-84) - George III (1738-1820) - RCIN 405307 - Royal Collection.jpg

name: Pope Benedict XVI
blurb: German theologian who served as pope from 2005 to 2013 (1927–2022) · became the first pope in almost 600 years to resign the office, stepping down in 2013 citing his failing strength of mind and body
source: Wikimedia Commons: Papst Benedikt XVI in Berlin 2011.jpg

name: Hirohito
blurb: Emperor of Japan through World War II and its aftermath (1901–1989) · renounced his own divinity in a 1946 radio address, and quietly published serious research papers on marine hydrozoa throughout his reign
source: Wikimedia Commons: Hirohito in dress uniform.jpg

name: Abraham
blurb: Patriarch revered as the founding father of Judaism, Christianity and Islam (traditionally c. 2000–1800 BC) · his near-sacrifice of his own son on Mount Moriah, halted at the last moment, is retold across all three faiths
source: Wikimedia Commons: Guercino Abramo ripudia Agar (cropped).jpg

name: Herbert Hoover
blurb: Thirty-first president of the United States, in office as the Great Depression began (1874–1964) · trained as a mining engineer, he had already made a fortune and fed millions of Belgian civilians as a WWI relief administrator before ever holding office
source: Wikimedia Commons: President Hoover portrait.jpg

name: Paul Newman
blurb: American actor known for Cool Hand Luke and The Sting (1925–2008) · founded the Newman's Own food brand as a joke among friends; it has since donated every cent of profit, over $500 million, to charity
attribution: Unknown author, dedicated to Bettmann Archive
source: Wikimedia Commons: Paul Newman - 1958.jpg
image_author: Unknown author, dedicated to Bettmann Archive

name: Virgin Mary
blurb: Central figure of Christian and Islamic tradition, mother of Jesus (traditionally 1st century BC – 1st century AD) · is the only woman named directly in the Quran, which devotes an entire chapter, Surah Maryam, to her
source: Wikimedia Commons: Duccio The-Madonna-and-Child-128.jpg

name: Saint Peter
blurb: Apostle regarded by the Catholic Church as its first pope (d. c. 64 AD) · tradition holds he asked to be crucified upside down, feeling unworthy to die in the same manner as Jesus
source: Wikimedia Commons: Pope-peter pprubens.jpg
